issues.legal_issue: A tenant cannot reopen an unappealed determination of the rent payable when that determination was subject to the applicable maximum rent.
material_facts: The landlord sought possession on the ground of rent defaults, and the rent payable was disputed.
The original authority determined the rent payable by reference to the applicable maximum rate and rejected the tenant’s asserted lower rent.
The tenant did not appeal that determination, which became final against the tenant.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not challenge the determined rent in the later proceedings; the rent found by the authority was the rent payable.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 6 and 7 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, rent agreed between landlord and tenant was payable subject to the maximum rate fixed under section 6. The unappealed factual determination of the rent payable could not be reopened by the tenant in the subsequent proceedings.

predicates.landlord_possession_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking possession on the ground that the tenant had failed to pay rent.
predicates.rent_payable_determined_by_authority: An authority determined the rent payable, taking account of the applicable limit on rent.
predicates.tenant_did_not_appeal_rent_determination: The tenant did not appeal the authority’s determination of the rent payable.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks possession for rent default and the tenant does not appeal an authority’s determination of rent, that determination remains binding on the tenant.

issues.legal_issue: Partial or late payment of rent in each of three years constitutes failure to pay rent for those years even when the total arrears are less than two years’ rent, provided arrears remain outstanding when possession is sought.
material_facts: The landlord sought possession for rent defaults covering three consecutive years.
For one year the tenant paid only part of the rent, for the next year the tenant paid nothing, and for the third year the tenant made only a partial payment after the payment period had expired.
Rent remained outstanding for all three years when the landlord sought possession, although the total arrears were less than the rent for two years.
issues.conclusion: The tenant had failed to pay rent for three years and was not entitled to relief allowing payment of the arrears to avoid forfeiture; the landlord was entitled to possession.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14 and 25(2) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, treat failure to pay rent within the prescribed period for any three years as excluding the relief available under section 25(1). Failure includes a partial failure to pay the rent due for a year, and does not depend on arrears exceeding two years’ rent. Under Raja Ram Mahadev Paranjype v. Aba Maruti Mali, a tenant in this position cannot obtain relief against forfeiture on equitable grounds or under section 114 of the Transfer of Property Act. Vithal Vasudeo Kulkarni v. Maruti Rama Nagane was explained as involving a different situation, in which no arrears remained outstanding when the possession application was made.

predicates.landlord_possession_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking possession because of the tenant’s rent defaults.
predicates.rent_not_fully_paid_within_required_peri: The tenant failed to pay the full rent due within the required period in each of three years, through partial or absent payment or payment after that period.
predicates.arrears_outstanding_when_possession_soug: Some rent arrears remained unpaid when the landlord sought possession.

issues.definition: If a landlord seeks possession, the tenant has not fully paid rent on time in each of three years, and arrears remain outstanding when possession is sought, the tenant cannot cure the default to avoid possession.
